{
  "research_question": "How do different stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) affect mouse navigation performance across five key metrics: Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "One-way ANOVA for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the fixed factor",
    "Logistic regression for binary response variable (Success) with Stim Paradigm as the predictor, followed by likelihood ratio test for overall significance"
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals for each continuous variable",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Levene's test for each continuous variable",
    "Independence: Assessed via experimental design (trials from different mice)",
    "For binary Success: Check for complete separation and assess model fit using deviance residuals"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "Tukey HSD for continuous variables if omnibus ANOVA is significant",
    "Pairwise comparisons with Bonferroni correction for logistic regression if overall test is significant"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham condition will show poorest performance across all metrics based on summary statistics",
    "Combined and Bright Visual Only paradigms will show best performance based on highest success rates and shortest times",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only will show intermediate performance",
    "Angular dispersion (AD) will be lowest in Sham condition indicating more direct paths despite poorer overall performance"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Uneven group sizes: Combined has 48,846 trials while Bright Visual Only has only 3,323",
    "Potential lack of normality in variables like Path Efficiency which shows extreme range (0.000928 to 29.817)",
    "Binary Success variable requires different analytical approach than continuous variables",
    "Potential clustering effects from multiple trials per mouse not accounted for in one-way ANOVA"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Mixed-effects modeling with Mouse as random effect to account for repeated measures within subjects, followed by contrast analysis between specific paradigm pairs of interest"
}
